title: Risk identification
ai_prompt:
You are an AI governance specialist completing Risk Identification (Step 5) for an AI use case that has already been classified (Step 3) and had a DPIA completed (Step 4).

CONTEXT — paste the full Stage 1 report (classification and DPIA) below this line, then run the prompt:

[PASTE STAGE 1 REPORT HERE]

---

This framework has 17 risks. Each risk maps to exactly ONE EU AI Act article and is treated by a set of harmonised-standard (HS) requirements. For every risk you will do two things:

  • STEP A — decide whether the risk APPLIES (yes / partially / no), using its category question.
  • STEP B — for risks that apply, list which HS REQUIREMENTS apply, by their ref. These are the requirements the system must implement and later evidence.

HOW MANDATORY WORKS: The SYSTEM CLASSIFICATION above lists the EU AI Act articles that apply to this use case. Any risk whose article is in that list is MANDATORY — answer its category question "yes". Concentrate your judgement on (a) which requirements apply within each applicable risk, and (b) risks whose article the classification did NOT trigger — decide those on what the system actually does. Output every risk key either way. Default to selecting ALL of an applicable risk's requirements unless one is clearly not relevant.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Your ENTIRE response must be ONLY the RISK ASSESSMENT SUMMARY JSON block at the end. Put your justification in the "reasoning" field (2–4 sentences per risk, specific to this system, no boilerplate — it is published verbatim in the report). Output nothing outside the JSON block.

===================================================================
RISKS
===================================================================


---

R01 — Opaque system to deployers  (Article 13)  (JSON key: RISK-001)
Risk: Opaque system to deployers — deployers lack the purpose, limitations and instructions needed to use the system correctly.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  User Documentation: Do system operators need documentation to understand any of the following?
  a) What the system is capable of doing
  b) The system's known limitations or blind spots
  c) Instructions for proper and safe usage
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 13 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Transparency]
    [18229-1.1] Intended Purpose — Clear, documented declaration of what the system is designed to do.
    [18229-1.2] Limitations — Documentation of known 'blind spots', error conditions, or scenarios where the AI may fail.
    [18229-1.3] Instructions for Use — High-quality documentation that is clear, accessible, and provided in a digital/readable format.

---

R02 — Ineffective human oversight  (Article 14)  (JSON key: RISK-002)
Risk: Ineffective human oversight — people cannot understand, question or halt the outputs, so they over-rely on the system.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Human Oversight: Do users interact with the system in a way that requires any of the following?
  a) Relying on the system to make or inform decisions
  b) The ability to understand and interpret the outputs
  c) The ability to override decisions or safely halt operations
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 14 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Human Oversight]
    [18229-1.6] Automation Confidence Warning — UI design that explicitly warns humans not to over-rely on AI suggestions.
    [18229-1.7] Intervention Tools — Inclusion of technical 'Override' or 'Stop' mechanisms (the 'Kill Switch').
    [18229-1.8] Interpretability — Ensuring outputs provide sufficient context for a human to understand the 'why' behind a decision.

---

R03 — Security compromise  (Article 15)  (JSON key: RISK-003)
Risk: Security compromise — the model, its data or its pipelines are attacked, corrupted or accessed without authorisation.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Cybersecurity: Is the system exposed to any of the following attack vectors?
  a) External or untrusted users
  b) Third-party data or models
  c) Public or networked infrastructure
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 15 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Threat Mitigation]
    [18282.1] Adversarial Attacks — Defense against 'evasion attacks' where crafted input data is designed to fool the model's logic.
    [18282.2] Data Poisoning — Protecting the training and RAG ingestion pipelines so malicious data doesn't corrupt the knowledge base.
    [18282.3] Model Inversion — Preventing 'extraction' attacks where unauthorized parties try to 'steal' the model or training data via API queries.
  [System Integrity]
    [18282.4] Secure Development — Procedures ensuring the code, RAG orchestrator, and model are built in a hardened, isolated environment.
    [18282.5] Supply Chain Security — Verifying the security and integrity of third-party libraries, pre-trained models, and external data sources.
  [Infrastructure]
    [18282.6] Access Control — Standard identity management (RBAC/MFA) for who can modify model weights or access proprietary data.
    [18282.7] Model Robustness — Ensuring the system remains secure and stable even when encountering 'noise' or unexpected data patterns.
  [Defense-in-Depth]
    [18282.8] Anomaly Detection — Continuous monitoring of AI inputs and outputs for signs of a cyberattack, such as prompt injection.

---

R04 — Inaccurate or unproven performance  (Article 15)  (JSON key: RISK-004)
Risk: Inaccurate or unproven performance — accuracy is not measured, validated, declared or monitored, so the system performs worse than believed.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Accuracy: Do any of the following apply to the system's outputs?
  a) Produces predictions
  b) Produces classifications
  c) Supports a task where output correctness is critical
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 15 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Metric Requirements]
    [18229-2.9] Metric Selection — Selecting the appropriate 'yardstick' (e.g., F1-score for classification or Mean Absolute Error for regression) for the specific use case.
    [18229-2.10] Validation — Rigorous testing to prove accuracy scores are not 'overfitted' to training data and remain valid on unseen data.
    [18229-2.11] Declaration — Explicitly stating the achieved accuracy levels and metrics within the formal Instructions for Use.
  [Lifecycle Performance]
    [18229-2.12] Consistency — Continuous monitoring to detect if accuracy 'drifts' or degrades after the system is in production.
    [18229-2.13] Benchmarking — Comparing AI performance against human expert benchmarks or recognized industry standards.
  [Technical Documentation]
    [18229-2.14] Verification Methods — Detailed documentation of the training/testing data split and the statistical methods used to verify results.

---

R05 — Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress  (Article 15)  (JSON key: RISK-005)
Risk: Fragile or unsafe behaviour under stress — the system fails unpredictably on noisy, shifting or adversarial conditions, or emits unsafe content.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Robustness: Must the system remain stable when facing any of the following?
  a) Corrupted or unexpected inputs
  b) Changing environmental conditions
  c) Adversarial inputs or usage
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 15 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Resilience Factors]
    [18229-2.15] Input Noise — Ensuring the AI can handle corrupted inputs (e.g., typos, sensor errors, or blurry data) without crashing.
    [18229-2.16] Environment Changes — Maintaining system functionality during external shifts, such as poor lighting or network latency.
    [18229-2.17] Feedback Loops — Implementing technical barriers to prevent the AI from learning from its own biased or incorrect outputs over time.
  [Fail-Safe Mechanisms]
    [18229-2.18] Graceful Degradation — Designing the system to fail safely (e.g., a 'safe state' or limited functionality mode) rather than an abrupt collapse.
    [18229-2.19] Technical Redundancy — Utilizing backup modules or 'sanity check' algorithms to catch and mitigate AI errors in real-time.
  [Reproducibility]
    [18229-2.20] Output Reliability — Ensuring the AI produces consistent, non-random outputs when given the exact same inputs.
  [Content Safety]
    [18229-2.21] Content Moderation Guardrail — Generated outputs pass through a content-safety classifier that blocks toxic, hateful, harassing, dangerous, or abusive content before delivery, and the guardrail is tested for resistance to jailbreak and prompt-injection attempts designed to elicit unsafe content.

---

R06 — Poor data quality & governance  (Article 10)  (JSON key: RISK-006)
Risk: Poor data quality & governance — the data driving the system is undocumented, unrepresentative, incomplete, inaccurate or unlawfully retained.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Data Quality: Do any of the following apply to the system's datasets?
  a) Performance depends on data quality or selection
  b) Uses data for training or fine-tuning
  c) Uses data for retrieval (RAG)
  d) Provenance and origin of the data affect outputs
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 10 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Governance Practices]
    [18284.1] Design Choices — Documenting the rationale behind data selection, including intended purpose and suitability assessments.
    [18284.2] Data Origin — Tracking the source and legal basis (provenance) of data collection and preparation.
    [18284.3] Data Preparation Operations — Standardizing processes for annotation, labeling, cleaning, enrichment, and aggregation.
  [Quality Metrics]
    [18284.4] Representativeness — Statistical proof (e.g., distribution analysis) that data reflects specific geographical, contextual, and behavioral settings.
    [18284.5] Completeness — Identifying and addressing 'data gaps' or missing information that could prevent regulatory compliance.
    [18284.6] Accuracy / Correctness — Implementing methods to detect and mitigate errors in labels and noise in the raw data.
  [Lifecycle Requirements]
    [18284.7] Dataset Splitting — Establishing strict rules for training, validation, and testing splits to ensure unbiased performance evaluation.
    [18284.8] Data Retention — Policies for storage duration (typically 10 years for documentation) and secure decommissioning mechanisms.
  [Assumptions]
    [18284.9] Formulation — Explicit documentation of what the data is intended to measure and represent (e.g., 'past history as a predictor').
  [Privacy Protection]
    [18284.10] Personal Data Egress & Output Filtering — Prompts and generated outputs are scanned for personal and confidential data and blocked or redacted before egress; the external model provider is contractually barred from retaining or training on submitted data, and data-loss-prevention controls are applied across the prompt and response path.

---

R07 — Discriminatory or biased outcomes  (Article 10)  (JSON key: RISK-007)
Risk: Discriminatory or biased outcomes — unfair results across groups because bias in the data or model is not detected or mitigated.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Bias & Fairness: Do any of the following apply to the system?
  a) Processes personal data about individuals
  b) Makes or informs decisions affecting people
  c) Could inadvertently treat demographic groups (age, gender, ethnicity, etc.) differently
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 10 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Bias Detection]
    [18283.1] Representativeness — Ensuring training, validation, and testing datasets proportionally cover all relevant subgroups (e.g., age, gender, ethnicity) to prevent under-representation bias.
    [18283.2] Bias Metrics — Applying specific mathematical tests, such as Disparate Impact or Equalized Odds, to provide a quantitative proof that the model does not favor one group over another.
    [18283.3] Proxy Identification — Identifying and analyzing 'hidden' variables (e.g., zip codes) that correlate with protected traits to prevent indirect discrimination.
  [Human & Social Context]
    [18283.4] Multi-stakeholder Input — Engaging diverse teams to define 'fairness' for specific use cases, ensuring the system respects different societal and functional settings.
    [18283.5] Fundamental Rights — Directly linking bias mitigation measures to the protection of fundamental rights and the prevention of discrimination prohibited under Union law.

---

R08 — Incomplete event recording  (Article 12)  (JSON key: RISK-008)
Risk: Incomplete event recording — the system does not immutably record the events needed to reconstruct what happened.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Logging: Does the system require a secure, unalterable audit trail for any of the following?
  a) System inputs and prompts
  b) Automated decisions and outputs
  c) System events and errors
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 12 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Logging]
    [18229-1.4] Event Recording — Automated, immutable recording of start/end times, input data, and all system decisions.
    [18229-1.5] Traceability — Ensuring logs allow for the full 'reconstruction' of events if a failure or accident occurs.

---

R09 — Inadequate system logging  (Article 12)  (JSON key: RISK-009)
Risk: Inadequate system logging — the system does not automatically record the events, inputs, states and errors needed to reconstruct and audit its behaviour.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Traceability: Must past system events be reconstructable for any of the following reasons?
  a) Routine audits or compliance checks
  b) Incident investigations or failure analysis
  c) Human oversight reviews
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 12 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Logging Triggers]
    [24970.1] Monitoring Events — Capturing automated performance benchmarks, safety checks, and anomalies triggered by the system's internal observability tools.
    [24970.2] Human Intervention — Recording every instance of a user overriding, editing, or stopping an AI output, directly linking to Article 14 oversight duties.
  [Captured Information]
    [24970.3] System State — Snapshots of current model parameters, version IDs, and configuration hashes at the exact time a decision or output was generated.
    [24970.4] Input/Output Data — Recording the specific user prompts and retrieved knowledge chunks that led to a high-risk or decision-making output.
    [24970.5] Errors & Failures — Detailed diagnostic data including error codes, messages, severity levels, and the fallback mechanisms activated during a crash.
  [Storage & Governance]
    [24970.6] Tamper Resistance — Using technical controls like Write-Once-Read-Many (WORM) storage or cryptographic hashes to ensure logs cannot be altered after creation.
    [24970.7] Retention Periods — Maintaining logs for at least 6 months (per Article 26(6)) or longer as mandated by sector-specific EU or national laws.
    [24970.8] Privacy — Balancing full traceability with GDPR requirements through data minimization, such as anonymizing user IDs where appropriate.

---

R10 — No quality management system  (Article 17)  (JSON key: RISK-010)
Risk: No quality management system — the organisation lacks the documented QMS to keep the AI conformant over its life.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Quality Management (QMS): Does your organization's role include any of the following?
  a) Acting as the original provider of a high-risk AI system
  b) Making substantial modifications to an existing AI system
  c) Operating under a formal Quality Management System
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 17 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Organizational Strategy]
    [18286.1] Compliance Strategy — A formal plan for how the organization will maintain conformity (including modifications to the AI).
    [18286.2] Accountability Framework — Defining clear roles and management responsibilities for AI safety.
  [Operational Controls]
    [18286.3] Design & Development — Procedures for design control, verification, and validation.
    [18286.4] Resource Management — Ensuring the right human and technical resources (e.g., compute power, specialized staff) are available.
  [Post-Launch Duties]
    [18286.5] Post-Market Monitoring (PMM) — A system to collect and analyze data on the AI's performance once it is in the hands of users.
    [18286.6] Incident Reporting — Procedures for reporting 'serious incidents' to national authorities within strict timelines.
  [Documentation & Records]
    [18286.7] Technical Documentation — Maintaining the 'Technical File' required by Article 11.
    [18286.8] Record-Keeping — Systems for storing logs and version-controlled documentation for at least 10 years.

---

R11 — Unmanaged risk lifecycle  (Article 9)  (JSON key: RISK-011)
Risk: Unmanaged risk lifecycle — the system's risks are not systematically identified, evaluated and mitigated across its life.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Risk Management: Does the system require risk management for any of the following phases?
  a) Initial design and development
  b) Continuous monitoring during its active lifecycle
  c) Documented mitigation of known and emerging risks
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 9 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Key Risk Iterations]
    [18228.1] Identification — Identification and analysis of known and reasonably foreseeable risks the AI system may pose to health, safety, or fundamental rights.
    [18228.2] Estimation — Estimation and evaluation of the risks that may emerge when the high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose or under conditions of reasonably foreseeable misuse.
    [18228.3] Evaluation — Evaluation of other emerging risks based on the analysis of data gathered from the post-market monitoring system.
  [Mitigation Hierarchy]
    [18228.4] Elimination — Elimination or reduction of risks as far as possible through adequate design and development.
    [18228.5] Mitigation — Implementation of appropriate mitigation and control measures in relation to risks that cannot be eliminated.
    [18228.6] Information — Provision of adequate information to deployers and, where appropriate, to persons likely to be affected by the system.

---

R12 — Incomplete technical file  (Article 11)  (JSON key: RISK-012)
Risk: Incomplete technical file — identity, architecture, training, performance and change history are not documented to a reviewable standard.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Technical Documentation: Do you need to produce a formal Technical File detailing any of the following?
  a) How the system was designed and built
  b) How the system was validated and tested
  c) How the system is version-controlled
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 11 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [System Description]
    [18286.9] System Identity & Purpose — Documented declaration of the system name, version, intended purpose, and the specific task it performs, as required by Annex IV point 1 of the AI Act.
    [18286.10] Architecture & Components — Description of the overall system architecture, key components, and the interactions between them, including any third-party models or services.
    [18286.11] Training Methodology — Documentation of the training approach, algorithms used, hyperparameters, and design choices made during development.
  [Performance Evidence]
    [18286.12] Accuracy & Metrics Achieved — Documented evidence of the accuracy levels and performance metrics achieved during testing, to be included in the instructions for use per Article 13.
    [18286.13] Testing & Validation Results — Summary of testing and validation outcomes including datasets used, test conditions, and results demonstrating the system meets its intended performance levels.
  [Change Management]
    [18286.14] Version Control — A versioning scheme is in place ensuring every release of the system is uniquely identified and traceable to its corresponding technical documentation.
    [18286.15] Modification Log — An auditable log of all changes made to the system after initial placement on the market, including the nature of the change and whether a new conformity assessment was triggered.

---

R13 — Unmanaged substantial modification  (Article 25)  (JSON key: RISK-013)
Risk: Unmanaged substantial modification — changes aren't evaluated for whether they trigger re-assessment or shift provider responsibility.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  System Modifications: Will the system undergo future updates involving any of the following?
  a) New models or significant architecture changes
  b) New retrieval data or training datasets
  c) Changes to the system's intended purpose
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 25 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Modification Assessment]
    [42001.1] Scope of Change Evaluation — A documented process exists to evaluate whether a proposed change to the AI system constitutes a substantial modification that affects the system's compliance with Chapter III Section 2 requirements.
    [42001.2] Provider Responsibility Trigger — Where a deployer makes a substantial modification outside the original provider's intended purpose, the process confirms that the modifier assumes provider responsibilities under Article 25.
  [Re-conformity]
    [42001.3] Re-assessment Requirement — A substantial modification triggers a full or partial re-run of the conformity assessment process under Article 43 before the modified system is redeployed.
    [42001.4] Updated Technical Documentation — The technical documentation under Article 11 is updated to reflect the modification, including revised architecture, performance evidence, and modification log entries.

---

R14 — Unmet deployer duties  (Article 26)  (JSON key: RISK-014)
Risk: Unmet deployer duties — the deployer doesn't operate per instructions, implement oversight, monitor/log, or assess affected persons.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Deployer Obligations: Does your organization's responsibility include any of the following?
  a) Acting as the deployer of a high-risk AI system
  b) Managing the system's day-to-day operation in production
  c) Ensuring the system is used according to the provider's instructions
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 26 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Operational Governance]
    [42001.5] Instructions for Use Compliance — The deployer operates the system strictly within the intended purpose and in accordance with the provider's instructions for use supplied under Article 13.
    [42001.6] Human Oversight Implementation — The deployer has assigned competent natural persons to perform human oversight of the system during operation, with the authority and capability to intervene or halt the system.
    [42001.7] Monitoring & Logging — The deployer monitors system operation and retains logs generated under Article 12 for the period specified by the provider or at least six months, and makes them available to authorities on request.
  [Impact Assessment]
    [42001.8] Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment — Prior to deployment in a public authority or regulated context, the deployer has conducted a fundamental rights impact assessment as required by Article 26(7), documented the findings, and notified the provider of any identified risks.
    [42001.9] Affected Persons Identification — The categories of natural persons and groups likely to be affected by the system's outputs have been identified, documented, and considered in the deployment design and oversight arrangements.

---

R15 — Unverified conformity  (Article 43)  (JSON key: RISK-015)
Risk: Unverified conformity — the system is deployed without a completed, signed-off conformity assessment.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Conformity Assessment: Is the system subject to any of the following pre-launch requirements?
  a) Being formally placed on the EU market
  b) Being put into service for its intended use
  c) Requiring a formal conformity assessment
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 43 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Pre-Market Review]
    [18286.16] Articles 9-17 Completion Verification — A structured internal review confirms that all applicable Article 9-17 controls in this framework have been assessed, that no controls remain in a Not Met status, and that evidence is available for each Applicable control.
    [18286.17] Competent Reviewer Sign-off — The self-assessment has been reviewed and approved by a person with sufficient technical and legal competence to evaluate conformity with the AI Act requirements, whose identity and qualifications are recorded.
  [Conformity Conclusion]
    [18286.18] No Critical Gaps Declaration — A formal written declaration confirms that no critical compliance gaps have been identified, or that all identified gaps have been resolved and re-assessed prior to market placement.
    [18286.19] Self-Assessment Conclusion Statement — A documented conclusion statement is produced confirming that the system meets all applicable requirements of Chapter III Section 2 of the AI Act and is ready for market placement or deployment.
  [Assessment Record]
    [18286.20] Conformity Review Date & Version — The date the conformity assessment was completed, the version of the system assessed, and the version of this compliance framework used are recorded and retained as part of the technical documentation.

---

R16 — Undisclosed AI interaction or content  (Article 50)  (JSON key: RISK-016)
Risk: Undisclosed AI interaction or content — people aren't told they're dealing with AI, or AI-generated content isn't labelled.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Transparency & Content Labeling: Does the system do any of the following?
  a) Simulate human interaction
  b) Generate synthetic content (text, images, audio, video)
  c) Manipulate content shown to users
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 50 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Disclosure Requirements]
    [12792.1] AI Identity Disclosure — Natural persons interacting with the system are informed in a clear, timely, and unambiguous manner that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from context.
    [12792.2] Disclosure Timing & Clarity — The AI disclosure is presented at the start of the interaction or before any consequential output is produced, and is expressed in plain language accessible to the intended audience.
  [Synthetic Content]
    [12792.3] AI-Generated Content Labelling — Content generated or manipulated by the system that could be mistaken for authentic human-created content is labelled as AI-generated in a machine-readable format and, where technically feasible, in a manner visible to the end user.
    [12792.4] Deep Fake Detection Support — Where the system generates synthetic audio, image, or video content depicting real persons or events, technical measures are in place to embed provenance metadata or watermarking to support downstream detection.
  [Deployer Duties]
    [12792.5] Deployer Disclosure Implementation — The deployer has implemented the provider's transparency instructions and can demonstrate that the disclosure mechanism is active in the production environment and has been tested for visibility and accessibility.

---

R17 — Blind post-market operation  (Article 72)  (JSON key: RISK-017)
Risk: Blind post-market operation — the live system isn't monitored, so drift, degradation and incidents go undetected.

STEP A — DOES THIS RISK APPLY? Answer the category question:
  Post-Market Monitoring: Will the live system require continuous monitoring to detect any of the following?
  a) Performance drift or data shifts
  b) System degradation over time
  c) Safety incidents or unexpected risks
  → If YES, this risk is MANDATORY (Article 72 applies to this use case).

STEP B — WHICH REQUIREMENTS APPLY? For a risk that applies, list in
selected_requirements the HS refs below whose requirement is relevant to
this system. Default to ALL of them unless one clearly does not apply.
  [Monitoring System]
    [18286.21] PMM Plan & Scope — A post-market monitoring plan is documented, covering the scope of monitoring, the data to be collected, the frequency of review, and the roles responsible for executing the plan.
    [18286.22] Performance Data Collection — The system actively collects performance data during operation, including accuracy metrics, error rates, and user feedback, sufficient to detect degradation or emerging risks over time.
    [18286.23] Drift & Degradation Detection — Automated or scheduled checks are in place to detect model drift, data distribution shift, or performance degradation, with defined thresholds that trigger a formal review or corrective action.
  [Feedback Loop]
